titleEn: Students creating documentaries with scientists deepens STEM belonging and public trust in science
titleZh: 学生与科学家共同拍摄纪录片，如何增强科学归属感与公众信任
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Marine scientists navigate autonomous glider robots across the Atlantic Ocean and along the West Antarctic Peninsula, collecting data to help predict storm intensity.
paragraphs.zh: 海洋科学家驾驶自主滑翔机机器人穿越大西洋并沿着西南极半岛飞行，收集数据以帮助预测风暴强度。

paragraphs.en: When farmers’ fields are destroyed by an unknown pathogen, plant scientists spend years breeding new varieties of disease-resistant food crops.
paragraphs.zh: 当农民的田地被一种未知的病原体摧毁时，植物科学家们花了数年时间培育抗病的粮食作物新品种。

paragraphs.en: A team of microbiologists explore deep-sea volcanoes in search of organisms that may contain anticancer compounds.
paragraphs.zh: 一组微生物学家探索深海火山，寻找可能含有抗癌化合物的生物。

paragraphs.en: These are passionate people who are dedicated to seeking solutions to real-world problems. They are also the main characters in science documentaries produced in the Rutgers Immersive Learning Science Storytelling Lab that I oversee. Our lab pairs students with working scientists to co-create documentaries about research as it happens, while earning experiential learning credit.
paragraphs.zh: 这些人充满激情，致力于为现实世界的问题寻求解决方案。他们也是我监督的罗格斯沉浸式学习科学讲故事实验室制作的科学纪录片中的主角。我们的实验室将学生与工作的科学家配对，共同创作关于研究的纪录片，同时获得体验式学习学分。

paragraphs.en: At a time when confidence in science is declining, I was approached by scientists who wanted their authentic research stories communicated to broad audiences.
paragraphs.zh: 在人们对科学的信心正在下降的时候，一些科学家找到我，希望将他们真实的研究故事传达给广大观众。

paragraphs.en: I am an educator, a researcher and anthropologist, and a science filmmaker who has been making science documentaries with Rutgers students and researchers since 2008. The science-in-action storytelling model I developed is intended to make the human journey of science visible to the public. Our stories communicate the process, motivations and integrity behind science, which helps earn public confidence and trust in science.
paragraphs.zh: 我是一名教育家、研究员和人类学家，也是一名科学电影制作人，自2008年以来一直与罗格斯大学的学生和研究人员一起制作科学纪录片。我开发的科学行动故事讲述模式旨在让公众了解人类的科学之旅。我们的故事传达了科学背后的过程、动机和完整性，这有助于赢得公众对科学的信心和信任。

paragraphs.en: I also partner with STEM learning researchers to gauge whether our documentaries increase the relatability of scientists, increase public understanding of scientific processes and help students find belonging in STEM.
paragraphs.zh: 我还与STEM学习研究人员合作，以衡量我们的纪录片是否增加了科学家的相关性，增加了公众对科学过程的理解，并帮助学生在STEM中找到归属感。

paragraphs.en: Our storytelling process
paragraphs.zh: 我们讲故事的过程

paragraphs.en: Science-in-action storytelling is composed of five steps that support student-scientist relationships.
paragraphs.zh: 科学在行动中讲故事是由五个步骤，支持学生与科学家的关系。

paragraphs.en: First, the storytellers develop trust with the participating university scientists. This trust stems from shared respect and a mutual understanding of the co-creation process.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，讲故事的人与参与的大学科学家建立信任，这种信任源于共同的尊重和对共同创造过程的相互理解。

paragraphs.en: The scientists then invite storytellers into their labs and field sites, where we capture their research processes in real time. This is Step 2.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，科学家们邀请讲故事的人进入他们的实验室和现场，在那里我们可以真实的捕捉他们的研究过程。这是第二步。

paragraphs.en: Our professional storytelling team, which includes students, then documents scientists conducting research, including experiments and data collection, as they describe the why and how of their work. Depending on the complexity of the project, we collect dozens to hundreds of hours of science-in-action video footage.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的专业讲故事团队，其中包括学生，然后记录科学家进行研究，包括实验和数据收集，因为他们描述了他们的工作的原因和方式。根据项目的复杂性，我们收集了几十到几百个小时的科学行动视频片段。

paragraphs.en: Importantly, this video data is maintained in our storytelling lab, as it often includes recordings of federally funded research. Maintaining the video data repository is a key component to establishing and sustaining trust with the participating scientists.
paragraphs.zh: 重要的是，这些视频数据保存在我们的讲故事实验室中，因为它通常包括联邦资助的研究记录。维护视频数据存储库是与参与科学家建立和保持信任的关键组成部分。

paragraphs.en: Step 3 invites students to immerse themselves in the video data and begin shaping the footage into documentary scenes, constructed using only the scientists’ words, without narration. As they analyze hours of footage, our students learn about the authentic scientific processes; in doing so, they participate in research through the process of storytelling.
paragraphs.zh: 第三步，让学生沉浸在视频数据中，开始将视频片段塑造成纪录片场景，只使用科学家的话语构建，不需要旁白。通过分析数小时的视频片段，我们的学生了解了真实的科学过程;在此过程中，他们通过讲故事的过程参与研究。

paragraphs.en: Our students are not graded on their documentary skills, nor are they required to make a film. Instead, they are graded on the science they learn through the storytelling process.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的学生不是根据他们的纪录片技能来评分的，也不要求他们制作电影。相反，他们通过讲故事的过程中学到的科学来评分。

paragraphs.en: Step 4 requires that the students share drafts of their documentary scenes with the featured scientist to verify the accuracy of the science communicated. This step is part of the foundational trust agreement with the scientists but is also an opportunity for the students to personally connect with scientists.
paragraphs.zh: 第四步要求学生与专题科学家分享他们的纪录片场景草稿，以验证所传达科学的准确性。这一步是与科学家达成的基础信任协议的一部分，也是学生与科学家个人联系的机会。

paragraphs.en: For Step 5, our lab works to distribute the documentaries to a wide variety of audiences, including the general public. Here we partner with STEM learning experts to assess audiences’ understanding of and trust in the science communicated in the film and audience perceptions of the featured scientists.
paragraphs.zh: 在第五步，我们的实验室致力于将纪录片分发给包括公众在内的各种观众。在这里，我们与STEM学习专家合作，评估观众对电影中传达的科学的理解和信任，以及观众对主要科学家的看法。

paragraphs.en: Reach far beyond the lab
paragraphs.zh: 远超实验室

paragraphs.en: Our completed science-in-action documentaries have reached audiences far beyond the university. Our National Science Foundation-funded “Antarctic Edge: 70° South” had a theatrical release and aired on Netflix. “Atlantic Crossing” was broadcast on PBS stations and was included in a three-year Smithsonian exhibit. “Fields of Devotion” was shared by the Association of American Universities as part of its campaign to increase public trust in science. And our lab’s newest long-form documentary, “Mysteries of 9° North,” co-created with 14 undergraduates and featuring scientists studying life at deep-sea volcanoes, will be released to the public in early 2027.
paragraphs.zh: 我们完成的科学纪录片已经达到了观众远远超出了大学。我们的国家科学基金会资助的“南极边缘：《南70度》在Netflix上上映，《大西洋彼岸》在PBS电视台播出，并被列入史密森尼博物馆为期三年的展览。被美国大学协会分享，作为其提高公众对科学信任的运动的一部分。我们实验室最新的长篇纪录片，“北纬9度，“与14名本科生共同创作，并以研究深海火山生命的科学家为特色，将于2027年初向公众发布。

paragraphs.en: Our surveys capture how these science documentaries change audience understanding of science and how it is done. For example, after screening “Antarctic Edge,” viewers’ self-reported understanding of climate change rose from 71% to 91%. On a 15-item knowledge quiz, average scores rose, with gains of up to 24 percentage points on the concepts they knew least about.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的调查捕捉到了这些科学纪录片如何改变观众对科学的理解，以及如何做到这一点。例如，在放映《南极边缘》后，观众自我报告的对气候变化的理解从71%上升到91%。在一项15项知识测验中，平均得分上升，在他们最不了解的概念上，平均得分上升了24个百分点。

paragraphs.en: Creating belonging for students in STEM
paragraphs.zh: 为STEM学生创造归属感

paragraphs.en: When 102 undergraduates were asked what made the scientists in “Fields of Devotion” relatable, they named passion for the subject (72%), desire to help others (71%) and commitment to their work (70%).
paragraphs.zh: 当102名本科生被问及是什么让“奉献领域”的科学家产生共鸣时，他们认为对该学科的热情（72%），帮助他人的愿望（71%）和对工作的承诺（70%）。

paragraphs.en: Our survey results also suggest that students who participated in the lab gained confidence and feelings of belonging in a science community. Undergraduates who once said they did not feel “smart enough” reported that they could now see themselves as scientists. All participating students reported that their collaboration with scientists positively transformed their understanding of science.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的调查结果还表明，参与实验的学生在科学社区中获得了信心和归属感。曾经认为自己“不够聪明”的本科生报告说，他们现在可以把自己视为科学家。所有参与实验的学生都报告说，他们与科学家的合作积极地改变了他们对科学的理解。

paragraphs.en: Nonscience majors gained a deep understanding of the scientific process, while science majors gained rare access to research outside their own disciplines.
paragraphs.zh: 非科学专业的学生对科学过程有了深刻的理解，而科学专业的学生很少有机会接触到自己学科之外的研究。

paragraphs.en: Student-directed science documentaries include “Growing the Caribbean Glider Fleet,” featuring scientists monitoring hurricane development; “Biting Back: The Lifesaving Potential of Catnip,” about the development of natural insect repellents; “Where Waters Meet on the Breathing Shore,” featuring climate scientists studying coastal ecosystems; “The B.A.S.I.L Project,” about USDA-funded plant-breeding research; “Ocean Farming,” about NOAA supported oyster breeding; “The Women of Nsongwe,” about USAID-supported agriculture projects in Zambia; and “Skycatcher,” about an NSF-funded atmospheric chemistry study in Alabama.
paragraphs.zh: 由学生指导的科学纪录片包括“加勒比滑翔机舰队的成长”，其中有科学家监测飓风的发展;“咬回来：猫薄荷的救生潜力”，关于天然驱虫剂的发展;“沃茨在呼吸海岸相遇”，其中有气候科学家研究沿海生态系统;“B.A.S.I.L项目”，关于美国农业部资助的植物育种研究;“海洋农业”，关于NOAA支持的牡蛎养殖;“恩松圭的妇女”，关于美国国际开发署支持的赞比亚农业项目;和“天空捕手”，关于国家科学基金会资助的亚拉巴马大气化学研究。

paragraphs.en: This science-in-action model offers a path forward that other universities could follow. Institutions can strengthen students’ STEM learning and science identities while training a new generation of credible, relatable voices for science.
paragraphs.zh: 这种科学在行动中的模式为其他大学提供了一条可以遵循的前进道路。机构可以加强学生的STEM学习和科学身份，同时培养新一代可信的、可联系的科学声音。

paragraphs.en: Uncommon Courses is an occasional series from The Conversation U.S. highlighting unconventional approaches to teaching.
paragraphs.zh: Uncommon Courses是The Conversation U.S.的一个偶然系列，突出了非传统的教学方法。
